feedback.end: Between 1517 and 1697, Spanish soldiers, known as conquistadors, invaded the Yucatán peninsula and began to destroy the Maya culture and its people.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: While the Maya were armed with long spears, bows and arrows, the Spanish invaders had artillery, steel swords and muskets.
The Spanish conquistadors also brought diseases to Mesoamerica that the Maya had never been exposed to before. The Maya reacted badly to these new diseases and lots of them died.

For centuries, the Spanish treated the Maya very badly and tried to get rid of their culture. They made them learn to speak Spanish and forced them to follow Christianity instead of their own religion.

feedback.end: As part of their strategy to eliminate Maya religion and culture, the conquistadors burned thousands of ancient Maya books and forced scribes to learn the Spanish writing system.

atoms.a: In which other ways do you think the Spanish tried to erase Maya religion and culture?

feedback.end: The Spanish invaders also pulled down sacred sites within Maya cities in their brutal campaign to spread Christianity.
